Node identity is SEMANTIC, not positional

Credential reads and script execs are first-class types.

128-dim memory vector per node, updated by a GRU cell
M[dst] ← GRU( cat( M[src], e, φ(t − τ[src]) ), M[dst] )
φ = 32-dim learned encoding of the inter-event interval
Memory module only — no attention over temporal neighbours.
This is not Rossi et al.'s full TGN and should not be described as one.
head 192→64→1 · 464,257 trainable parameters · 3 seeds averaged, ONE shared split
Fitted across all windows so it calibrates instead of assuming a trace length.
npm ships without it — the hybrid reproduced the TGN's predictions exactly.
A fixed-prefix model is out-of-distribution at every other length: trained only
at 3000 events it scored known malware at p=0.0001 when the live install
produced 1,900. The behavioural envelope corroborates; it does not decide.

Leakage audit — a gate, not a report
rejects any token present in ≥90% of one class and ≤10% of the other
rejects any single feature with disjoint class ranges
rejects differing capture environments across the split
Caught /dev/pts in 97.2% benign / 0% malicious — a one-line rule on it
scored 96.48% F1. Training is REFUSED on a corpus that fails.
feature normalisation fitted on train only; balanced batches
every threshold selected on VALIDATION; test scored exactly once
3 seeds (42 / 7 / 1337) averaged, all sharing ONE split via --split-seed
Per-member splits once leaked 145 of 210 test packages into siblings'
training data, inflating PyPI F1 to a withdrawn 93.22%.
Held-out results — test split, scored once
vs OSCAR (ASE '24): PyPI 91.00% F1 → SCBF +1.73 · npm 95.00% → SCBF −18.23
Live: PyPI 10/12 malware blocked, 10/10 clean · npm 6/10, 8/10
• 98 of 379 malicious npm packages declare NO install hook — they execute
nothing during install, so no install-time monitor can see them (AUC 0.688)
• benign traces came from local archives, so registry installs are falsely
blocked — a known defect, not a limitation
• 59 malicious PyPI / 57 npm test samples → F1 carries ≈ ±4%
